![](images/transform-your-future-at-the-microsoft-365-community-conference/body-001.jpg)

Welcome to the latest episode of [Polaris](https://polaris.synozur.com)! I'm excited to introduce our guests, **Jeff Teper**, President of Collaborative Apps and Platforms at Microsoft, and **Karuana Gatimu**, Director of M365 Customer Advocacy at Microsoft. Jeff and Karuana (and guests) are delivering the **keynote** for this year’s [Microsoft 365 Community Conference](https://m365conf.com/), May 6-8, 2025 at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas, Nevada.

  
  

As we gear up for the conference, it was great to sit down with Jeff and Karuana to review the transformative journey that has led us here. We delved into what they'll be bringing to this year's keynote and provided a sneak peek into what you can expect.

  

![](images/transform-your-future-at-the-microsoft-365-community-conference/body-002.jpg)![](images/transform-your-future-at-the-microsoft-365-community-conference/body-002.jpg)![](images/transform-your-future-at-the-microsoft-365-community-conference/body-003.png)![](images/transform-your-future-at-the-microsoft-365-community-conference/body-003.png)

**Jeff Teper and Karuana Gatimu**

  

The **M365 Community Conference** highlights the latest innovations from Microsoft and offers over 200 sessions, workshops, lightning talks, roundtables, panels, and keynotes. Topics covered include Copilot, agents, Teams, Viva, SharePoint, OneDrive, Power Platform, and more.

![](images/transform-your-future-at-the-microsoft-365-community-conference/body-004.jpg)

Jeff shared his insights into the evolution of Microsoft 365, emphasizing the importance of community and collaboration in driving technological advancements. Karuana, with her expertise in user adoption and change management, offered a unique perspective on how individuals and organizations can leverage these innovations to transform their futures.

  

### Key Points:

The **Microsoft 365 Community Conference** is an annual event that brings together thousands of Microsoft business and technology professionals.

You can register now and save $150 with the registration code **SAVE150**

  

[

Register Now!

](https://nextgen365events.com/#!/register/?utm_term=SAVE150)

  

### Conference History…and your story

Jeff also reflected on the evolution of the conference, emphasizing its significance for enthusiasts of M365 and Copilot. The first **SharePoint Conference** was held in 2008, with Bill Gates announcing the upcoming releases of SharePoint Online and Exchange Online. This conference has a rich history, growing to become a significant event across all Microsoft 365, Power Platform and more, for business and technology professionals.

  

And this community is more than just tech. We want to add your story to that history. Today, Microsoft and Synozur are **launching a program** to capture your conference story from the M365 Conference or SPC. We’re building an oral history of the event, and we want to get **your** story.

  
  

Learn more about it in this week’s [post on the Insights blog](https://www.synozur.com/post/it-s-time-for-your-conference-story) or the [Microsoft Tech Community](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/CommunityNewsDesk/share-your-conference-story/4402401). We can’t wait to hear from you!

  

### Polaris

**Polaris**, the Synozur podcast, charts the course for business and technology transformation.

![](images/transform-your-future-at-the-microsoft-365-community-conference/body-005.jpg)

  

Additionally, [Synozur](https://www.synozur.com) is proud to [sponsor and deliver sessions](https://aka.synozur.com/M365CC-2025) at the conference and our booth at this year's Expo.

  

Polaris is available on [Apple](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/polaris-pathways-a-synozur-podcast/id1773172041), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/show/1cEtlJsybYcFFGTiKU1pX6?si=6faafd668eb44d5b), [Amazon](https://music.amazon.com/podcasts/db9939ac-8343-420e-97c3-ee09eae50c74/polaris-pathways---a-synozur-podcast), [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@SynozurVideos) or wherever you get your favorite podcasts.  It’s produced with the help of our friends at [Riverside.fm](http://Riverside.fm). Our theme song, “_Alternative Dream_” is provided courtesy of [Adobe](https://www.adobe.com).  Additional music and sound provided by IndieGuy Records. Graphic design by Josh Brantley.

  

## Show Notes

  

## References

Any time we speak with Jeff and Karuana, you can expect a fairly extensive reference and reading list.

  

### News and Data

Live events are back.  According to [Allied Market Research](https://truelist.co/blog/event-industry-statistics/), after most events disappeared in 2020 and 2021, the events industry is expected to reach $1,552.9 billion by 2028, growing at more than 11% annually.

Learning how to apply AI correctly is crucial. McKinsey is projecting generative AI can add over $4.4 trillion in corporate profits, with significant boosts to productivity form AI and automations [Source: McKinsey](https://www.mckinsey.com/mgi/overview/in-the-news/ai-could-increase-corporate-profits-by-4-trillion-a-year-according-to-new-research)

  

### Microsoft 365 Community Conference 2025

Visit the [official website](https://www.m365conf.com/) to learn more and get $150 off registration with the code SAVE150

Microsoft’s [quick guide to the M365 Conference](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/spblog/sharepoint-at-the-microsoft-365-community-conference/4399317) from Mark Kashman

  

### History of the M365 Conference and SharePoint Conference

It’s [Microsoft’s 50th anniversary](https://news.microsoft.com/microsoft-50/), so we’re also looking back at key moments in the history of this conference and its predecessor. We’re building an oral history from its origins in 2008 as the SharePoint Conference through 2025.   You can [share your story](https://aka.synozur.com/m365-stories) and we’ll compile the best for future podcasts on [Polaris](https://polaris.synozur.com) and from [Microsoft](https://intrazone.libsyn.com).

  

Here are some highlights over the years.

-   [Bill Gates kicked off](https://news.microsoft.com/speeches/bill-gates-sharepoint-conference-2008/) the very first SharePoint Conference (SPC) in March 2008 by announcing availability for SharePoint Online and Exchange Online
    
-   [Huey Lewis and the news](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mfa0uxGLZmE) were the entertainment highlights at SPC in October 2009
    
-   SPC 2011 was held at Disneyland in Anaheim, CA, and people literally [danced](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eUU0KJ-w2bc) to get in.
    
-   Did we mention [Gangnam Style](https://azalea-conch-fcsz.squarespace.com/insights/m365-conference-2025-history#:~:text=Dux%20Raymond%20Sy%20performing%20%E2%80%9CGangnam%20Style%E2%80%9D%2C%202012) in 2012?
    
-   It wasn’t “SPC” but Microsoft set the stage for a decade of cloud innovation at the “[Future of SharePoint](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/blog/2016/05/04/the-future-of-sharepoint/)” event in San Francisco, May 4, 2016.
    
-   Jeff also reflected on the [return of SPC in 2018](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yb43DQNBTgY), and getting s to share the [B-52s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZWofj8uIEYI) with everyone.
    

  

### Microsoft Resources & Updates

-   [Microsoft Tech Community](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/) – home for discussions, resources and blogs across all Microsoft technologies.
    
-   [CommunityDays.org](http://CommunityDays.org) – Odds are good there’s ’a Microsoft community event happening near you soon – and this site can tell you where and when,
    
-   [SharePoint Hackathon Spring 2025](https://github.com/sharePoint/sharepoint-hackathon) Details on GitHub, and award winners will be recognized in May 2025 at M365CC.
    
-   [January 2025 SharePoint Event](https://aka.ms/SharePointEvent) – the latest updates on AI, agents and page designs for your intranet.
    
-   Most recently, Microsoft released their new [Researcher and Analyst](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/blog/2025/03/25/introducing-researcher-and-analyst-in-microsoft-365-copilot/) agent to develop deep, rich answers to complex questions, as Jeff discussed on the show.
    

  

### Culture References

Some of the games and TV shows covered include:

-   [The Pitt](https://www.max.com/shows/pitt-2024/e6e7bad9-d48d-4434-b334-7c651ffc4bdf) on HBO Max features Noah Wyle from ER in his return to medical television. Recommended by Jeff. 
    
-   [Hacks](https://www.max.com/shows/hacks/67e940b7-aab2-46ce-a62b-c7308cde9de7) is also on HBO Max, and recommended by Karuana.
    
-   [Severance](https://tv.apple.com/us/show/severance/umc.cmc.1srk2goyh2q2zdxcx605w8vtx) on Apple TV has been a brain teaser for many of us this year.  What exactly is “Macro Data Refinement”? And if you want to try moving numbers around on a screen for fun, [Sudoku](https://www.nytimes.com/puzzles/sudoku) may be as close as you get. Until you try [the Lumon MDR web site](https://codepen.io/cobra_winfrey/full/ogvpYwv).
    

  

### Events

-   [M365 Philly](https://www.communitydays.org/event/2025-04-26/m365-philly-2025) | April 26, 2025 (Microsoft Innovation Hub in Malvern PA)
    
-   [Microsoft 365 Community Conference](https://m365conf.com/#!/) | May 5-8, 2025 (Vegas)
    
-   [Microsoft Build](https://build.microsoft.com/en-US/home) | May 19-22, 2025 (Seattle Convention Center)
    
-   [TechCon 365 Seattle](https://www.techcon365.com) | June 23-27, 2025 (Seattle Convention Center)
    
      
    

### Takeaways

-   The Microsoft 365 Community Conference is the best place to connect with the best community in technology today.
    
-   Community engagement is crucial for personal and professional growth.
    
-   Understanding the 'why' behind technology enhances its value.
    
-   Networking at conferences can significantly impact careers.
    
-   Microsoft fosters a culture of support and opportunity.
    
-   The conference will showcase new features and innovations.
    

  

### Sound Bites

“We can't wait to see everyone there."

  

#### Jeff Teper

-   One thing that's great about this place is we can reflect and celebrate and be nostalgic, but don't feel like you need any of that shared history. Let's go invent the future together. And this will be the best place to do that too. Not just celebrate.
    
-   It is just unbelievable to work in a team on a product that has that kind of impact on people. I mean, you're supposed to leave the planet better than you found it. And it's not just about winning some technology race. It's about helping people have a sense of fulfillment and purpose that really, at the end of the day, gets me most motivated.
    
-   Sometimes I'm up there thinking, if there's one person, just one person in the room who has no idea why they showed up to this conference, their boss made them and they're sitting like, what is this thing? If we can inspire that one person to use technology, to have an impact on others so they can have an impact on themselves, that's kind of what we're trying to do.
    

  

#### Karuana Gatimu

-   We have a community lounge…and there we have a tremendous amount of meetups, a facilitated way that you can meet other IT professionals. We'll have community reporters throughout the event, doing interviews and recaps. We'll have some fantastic interviews with the product group folks.

bodyHtml:
In our latest episode of Polaris, "The Productivity Paradox: Handling More with Less," we delve into the pressing issue of productivity in the modern workforce.


Mark Struczewski, our guest for this episode, shares valuable insights on how to manage the ever-growing demands for more projects, new apps, and constant engagement, all while grappling with the constraints of time – our scarcest resource.  Mark – aka “Mr. Productivity” - discusses practical strategies to boost productivity, enhance efficiency, and ensure that we can keep up with the relentless pace of the business world.

One key point Mark emphasizes is the importance of a growth mindset. By consistently seeking improvement and embracing challenges, we can adapt to new demands and thrive in our professional lives.


You can follow up with Mark through his website, https://misterproductivity.com/ or on LinkedIn.


Polaris is available on Apple, Spotify, Amazon, YouTube or wherever you get your favorite podcasts. Thanks for tuning in, and don't forget to leave a positive review on Apple podcasts. Our contest will run from now through May 1st, so participate and spread the word!


Polaris is produced with the help of our friends at Riverside.fm. Our theme song, “Alternative Dream” is provided courtesy of Adobe.  Additional music and sound provided by IndieGuy Records. Graphic design by Josh Brantley.


References


Mr. Productivity

You can follow up with Mark through his website, https://misterproductivity.com/ or on LinkedIn.


One of Mark’s favorite pieces of pop culture is the time management book The 5AM Club: Own Your Morning. Elevate Your Life.: Sharma, Robin: 9781443456623: Amazon.com: Books


Impact of Digital Distractions on Productivity

According to a study by RescueTime, the average worker spends only 2 hours and 48 minutes per day on productive tasks. The rest of the time is often consumed by digital distractions such as social media, emails, and other non-work-related activities. Source: RescueTime


A report by Udemy found that 70% of workers feel distracted during work hours, with 16% stating that they are almost always distracted. Source: Udemy


Rise of AI Tools in Enhancing Productivity

A recent report by McKinsey & Company highlights that AI adoption has the potential to increase global productivity by up to 1.4% annually. Source: McKinsey & Company


Growing Importance of Personalized Productivity Coaching

The demand for personalized productivity coaching has surged, especially with the shift to remote work. A survey by the International Coach Federation (ICF) found that 89% of coaching clients reported improved work performance and 70% reported improved time management skills. Source: ICF


Multitasking

Think you’re a great multitasker? Read on to learn why you’re probably not as good as you think. Opinion | A Focus on Distraction - The New York Times


Events

Microsoft 365 Community Conference | May 5-8, 2025 (Vegas) .

European Collaboration Summit | May 26-28, 2025 (Düsseldorf, Germany)

TechCon 365 Seattle | June 23-27, 2025


Sound Bites

  • "FOMO is real. We don't want to wait."

  • "Attention residue is real."

  • "Everybody procrastinates."

  • "You can either fight AI or use it."

  • "Productivity isn't about doing more; it's about doing what matters most."

  • "Efficiency comes from smart strategies, not just hard work."


Takeaways

  • Many people feel overwhelmed due to constant technology bombardment.

  • Prioritization is key to achieving goals.

  • Reviewing daily tasks can enhance productivity.

  • Writing things down can relieve cognitive load.

  • People often switch productivity tools unnecessarily.

  • Technology can both aid and hinder productivity. Attention residue affects our ability to focus on tasks.

  • Defining personal success is crucial for motivation and productivity.

  • Procrastination is a common human experience that everyone faces.

  • Establishing boundaries between work and personal life is essential.

  • Buffer time between meetings can reduce stress and improve focus.

  • Effective time management is key to maximizing productivity.

bodyHtml:
We’re collecting an oral history of the Microsoft 365 Community Conference


It’s about a month until the biggest event of the year for the Microsoft 365 community - the M365 Community Conference in Las Vegas, May 6-8.


In March 2008, Bill Gates kicked off the first ever Microsoft SharePoint Conference (“SPC”) in Redmond, WA. Since then, SPC has evolved into the annual don’t-miss M365 event for the best community in tech.

Whether it’s M365CC or WPC, this event has history.  So many cloud innovations were first introduced during keynotes. We’ve had so many great speakers and entertainers over the years: Jeff Teper, Jared Spataro, Elvis Presley, Bill Clinton, Huey Lewis, Jon Bon Jovi, the B-52‘s, Danica Patrick, and many more.


Synozur is proud to be sponsoring and speaking this year. Today, we’re launching a program with Microsoft to capture your conference story from the M365 Conference or SPC. We’ve seen flash mobs and funerals, beach parties and dance parties. But that’s not all. We want to get your story.

 

We've set up this voice box to allow you to record your story, or you can just send it to us at polaris@synozur.com. Please share your contact details.


If you had a hand in finding a coffin in Las Vegas, or wondered about the flash mob in Anaheim, or a late-night pool party in Florida, we’d like to hear more.

What was your first conference like? What was your first speaking event like?  Is there a friend you met for the first time at one of our events?  Favorite dinners? Favorite parties? Any memorable trips away from the venue? All stories are welcome.


We'll edit the best stories together for a future broadcast on the Polaris podcast - and we may invite some of you for a live interview for the Intrazone podcast.


Thanks. We look forward to sharing your story for the history of the Microsoft 365 Conference.  


Synozur at Microsoft 365 Community Conference.

Remember, you can get $100 off registration by using the SYNOZUR100 code at checkout.


Here are some of our sessions at the event:

  • Information Architecture (IA) for Enterprise AI (Michelle Caldwell / Chris McNulty)

  • Upgrade Your Company Operating System with Microsoft Viva (Chris McNulty)

  • From Scratch to Spectacular: Starting Out with Power Pages (Shari Oswald)

  • Quick, Creative, and Compelling: Unleash Clipchamp to emPOWER! Your eLearning! (Shari Oswald)

title: Why AI?
excerpt: AI lacks intrinsic human values and requires human intervention to ensure ethical and accurate outputs.
bodyHtml:
Or why humans still matter


Summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly Generative AI (GenAI), lacks intrinsic human values and requires human intervention to ensure ethical and accurate outputs. Despite its ability to simulate intelligence through Large Language Models (LLMs), GenAI can produce flawed and harmful content due to its dependence on open Internet data. The human end user must guide and refine AI outputs to maintain appropriateness and veracity, highlighting the ongoing importance of human oversight in AI development.

One would have to be a hermit or comatose to be completely unaware of the growing controversy over the use of chatbots and so-called Generative AI (GenAI). The computer models for these types of AI are based on Large Language Models (LLMs) and are considered by many to be inherently flawed.

 

The LLM concept is relatively simple, although its execution is not: scrape all possible content off the open Internet, use advanced neural network processing to determine the most common patterns found there, and then use the most likely connections to parrot back statistically relevant information in a very human-consumable way, presented to the user as “intelligence”. This is how the AI is “trained”.

 

However, that core compute model has no heart, no ethical principles, and no humanity, by which I mean no simulacrum of compassion, empathy, or caring. By geometrically increasing the processing power by which linkages and likely outcomes are computed, it does create a simulacrum of “intelligence”, by which I mean plausible and potentially useful responses which represent a consensus summary or detail on any particular topic.

 

It uses the interpolated patterns of grammar to render its responses human-friendly, but it can get its utterances wrong, sometimes very wrong. Those seemingly random ramblings which veer off a logical path are often called ‘hallucinations” but are more accurately called dissociated reasoning.

 

Even the most current GenAI platforms must be ‘disciplined’ by human minders, to adjust the relative value of specific attributes (“weights”) so that they better reflect core human values (e.g., kindness or politeness) and avoid amplifying human weakness (e.g. cruelty or exploitation).

 

Unfortunately, these guardrails are not intrinsic to the models themselves, as the models are again built on the open Internet, whereby Hitler’s Mein Kampf, bombmaking recipes, or paranoid extremism are just another type of content harvested, along with the Bible, Shakespeare, and the Bhagavad Gita.

 

No AI currently available can extrapolate human values extrinsically from Internet content – which is the broadest body of data (“corpus”) in human history. And the current LLM approach is very unlikely to ever get us there, no matter how many GPUs we throw at it.

 

This is where the human end user can and must play an essential role: to guide, aid, edit, or reframe the GenAI output as they see fit. Using a powerful chatbot or GenAI platform is akin to having an army of inexperienced but industrious interns at your fingertips – they can save you hours or days of tedious research and fact-finding. But it is up to you, not the bot, to determine appropriateness, accuracy, and veracity. Just as it would be for the manager of human interns.

 

The danger here is that the global race to become a dominant AI platform is rendering the humanist principles as ‘nice-to-have’, not core. Again, the models are lacking basic human values as intrinsic to their data interpolation and projections, and human minders are expensive, especially at scale.

 

There is an inherent drive to lower cost in the capitalist economic model (“value extraction”), and without self-restraint this can lead to an acute devaluing of the human factor – resulting in job dislocation, greater economic instability, and accelerated wealth concentration among a select few. This is not viable for long term societal peace and equilibrium.

 

Again, this dystopian outcome points back to the human factor. It’s not really the AI which is the problem – it’s how we choose to use it that will be drive future outcomes. One can just as easily imagine the use of GenAI to further and foster a human economic and cultural apotheosis. As Charlton Heston declaimed at the end of the film Soylent Green, the answer “…is people!”

title: The Booming Content Management Market: Insights and Projections for 2025-2028
excerpt: Content management market size will reach $31 to $150 billion by 2028, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 14.1%.
bodyHtml:
The content management market, evolving from traditional ECM to advanced Content Services, is crucial for organizational efficiency and innovation, especially with the rise of AI. Future projections indicate robust growth driven by emerging technologies and diverse applications, with the market size expected to reach $31 to $150 billion by 2028, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 14.1%.


Unveiling the Growth and Future Trends

ECM, content services, content management, document management – whatever you call it, it’s the lifeblood of your organization. Your content represents the creativity, decisions, transactions and culture of your organization. It’s your intellectual property. It’s what makes you, you.


Content is essential for learning, decisions, and transactions. It’s at the center of most workflows and structured processes. And in the era of generative AI, having the “right” content for your LLMs is mission-critical to get a return on your AI investments.


In the ever-evolving landscape of digital transformation, content management stands as a pillar of organizational efficiency and innovation. At Synozur, we are committed to providing innovative insights, drawing from our proprietary research and the latest industry data.


In this article, I’ll survey the current and future state of the market, and project its growth over the coming years. For consistency, we’ll call this the “Content Management” market.


Understanding the Content Management Market

The content management market has its roots in traditional Enterprise Content Management (ECM), which focused on storage, metadata workflow, records management, and search for on-premises repositories. Historically described as "systems of record," ECM was often seen as an expensive way to store high-volume content that was rarely accessed again.


Over the past decade, ECM has evolved into Content Services (CS), leveraging cloud capabilities and AI to offer more flexible and integrated solutions that encompass dynamic content, collaboration, and emerging data types like images and video. Today, the market encompasses a broad array of applications, including archiving software, document generation, content-driven solutions, and eDiscovery, among others.


More recently, Tim Nelms, Marko Sillanpaa, Max Goss, and Chris Jackson at Gartner have published their latest Magic Quadrant for Document Management . They’ve expanded the definition to include generative AI and other emergent workloads. And they’ve added yet another name – document management – to the market sector. Microsoft, Box, Laserfiche, SER Group and OpenText were all recognized as Leaders, with Google, M-Files, Dropbox, and Hyland as Challengers.



Market Size and Growth Projections

The content management market is substantial, with significant growth projected over the next few years.


By the narrowest definition, we could define content management as just two sectors – content sharing and ECM – and reach a current market size of US$16.3 billion. Let’s consider those sectors. They may include additional processing services, management, and content driven applications. A full set of those sectors may include:


  • Archiving Software

  • Capture Applications

  • Content Sharing and Collaboration

  • Content Workflow

  • Content-Driven Applications (e.g., Contract Lifecycle Management, Digital Asset Management, Sales Force Automation)

  • Document Generation Software

  • Document Understanding AI

  • eDiscovery Applications

  • Enterprise Backup and Recovery

  • Enterprise Content Management

  • eSignature Software

  • Intelligent Document Processing (IDP)

  • Repository Services

  • Workplace Search


Key Market Segments

Many critical market sectors are growing significantly, especially with generative AI-related effects and the need for more comprehensive content-driven applications. Several key segments drive the content management market, each with unique growth trajectories:

  • Enterprise Backup and Recovery: Estimated to grow from $14.3 billion in 2024 to $23.5 billion by 2028, with a CAGR of 13.8%.

  • Document Understanding AI: One of the fastest-growing segments, expected to double from $3.2 billion in 2023 to $6.1 billion by 2027, with a CAGR of 17.8%.

  • Contract Lifecycle Management: Expected to grow from $2.3 billion in 2024 to $3.7 billion by 2028.

  • Sales Force Automation: Projected to increase from $10.9 billion in 2024 to $16.1 billion by 2028.

  • Digital Asset Management: Anticipated to expand from $5.6 billion in 2024 to $9.8 billion by 2028.


So, the current size of the market in 2025 ranges from US$24 billion to about US$110 billion, based on what sectors you choose. For these definitions, we start with a “Narrow” view of the market (ECM, content sharing and on-premises), with a “Broad” range that includes other sectors and an “Expansive” view that includes everything except generative AI[1]:


 

This gives us the following market sizes (in $USMM):

ECM, content services, content management, document management – whatever you call it, it’s the lifeblood of your organization. Your content represents the creativity, decisions, transactions and culture of your organization. It’s your intellectual property. It’s what makes you, you.

In this article, I’ll survey the current and future state of the market, and project its growth over the coming years. For consistency, we’ll call this the “Content Management” market.

  

## Understanding the Content Management Market

The content management market has its roots in traditional Enterprise Content Management (ECM), which focused on storage, metadata workflow, records management, and search for on-premises repositories. Historically described as "systems of record," ECM was often seen as an expensive way to store high-volume content that was rarely accessed again.

  

Over the past decade, ECM has evolved into Content Services (CS), leveraging cloud capabilities and AI to offer more flexible and integrated solutions that encompass dynamic content, collaboration, and emerging data types like images and video. Today, the market encompasses a broad array of applications, including archiving software, document generation, content-driven solutions, and eDiscovery, among others.

title: Polaris: Walk the Project Runway with Michelle Boyd
excerpt: In this episode of Polaris, Chris McNulty and Michelle Boyd discuss the importance of delivery excellence in project management.
bodyHtml:
Polaris brings you insightful discussions and expert opinions on business transformation, leadership culture, and strategic markets. In our latest episode, we cover successful project and delivery management to help you navigate and succeed in today's demanding environment. This week I sat down with Michelle Boyd, head of Delivery Excellence at Synozur.



Michelle's fascinating career spans construction, business school, and global consulting, bringing a wealth of knowledge and experience to the table.


All episodes are shared on our Polaris page. You can also find us on Apple, Spotify, Amazon, or wherever you get your favorite podcasts. And you can subscribe to be alerted when we add new episodes.

Episode Highlights

  • Dive deep into the RAIDD (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, Dependencies, Decisions) log and learn how to effectively manage these critical elements in your project.

  • Project Rescue: Discover the initial steps to take when rescuing a project that has gone off track.

  • New Technologies in Project Delivery: Explore the latest technologies revolutionizing project delivery and their impact on your workflow.

  • Delivery Management Success: Gain insights into the key factors that contribute to successful delivery management.

  • Examine a real-world case study showcasing successful project delivery.


Expert Insights and Data Points

According to a recent report by the Project Management Institute, organizations that prioritize delivery management are 30% more likely to meet their goals and stay within budget.  Source: Pulse of the Profession | PMI


Agile methodologies, traditionally used in software development, are now being adopted by various industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and construction. A study by McKinsey & Company found 75% of organizations in these sectors have implemented agile practices to improve efficiency and adaptability. Source: 17 Agile Statistics You Need to Know in 2025


Another trend is the intersection of AI and project management. Gartner predicts by the end of this year, AI will automate 80% of project management tasks, leading to increased productivity and reduced human error. [They’ve changed this recently to a 2030 target, FYI.]  Source: AI in project management: A no hype guide for teams


Don't miss out on these invaluable insights! Subscribe to Synozur's Polaris podcast and join us on the journey to delivery excellence.


Show Notes

Takeaways

  • Delivery excellence is crucial for organizations.

  • A project is defined as a temporary endeavor with specific objectives.

  • Miscommunication is often the root cause of project failures.

  • Kickoff meetings are essential for aligning expectations and success criteria.

  • Agile methodologies are not always the best fit for every project.

  • Technology can enhance project management but is not a panacea.

Sound Bites

  • "Projects are more about people than processes."

  • "Flexibility within a framework is the true essence of effective project management."

  • "Technology should be an enabler, not a dictator, of project success."

  • “That person who went on leave three months became a hidden stakeholder. Those folks can be a real problem as you go through delivery. Kickoff meetings can mitigate that.”

 

 

References

The Rise of Agile Methodologies in Non-Software Industries:

According to a recent report by the Project Management Institute (PMI), organizations that prioritize delivery management are 30% more likely to meet their project goals and stay within budget. This highlights the critical role of delivery management in achieving project success. Source: Pulse of the Profession | PMI


Agile methodologies, traditionally used in software development, are now being adopted by various industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and construction. A study by McKinsey & Company found that 75% of organizations in these sectors have implemented agile practices to improve efficiency and adaptability. Source: 17 Agile Statistics You Need to Know in 2025


The Impact of AI and Automation on Project Management:

The integration of AI and automation tools in project management is transforming the way projects are planned, executed, and monitored. Gartner predicted that by 2025, AI will automate 80% of project management tasks, leading to increased productivity and reduced human error. [They now say it will take until 2030.] Source: AI in project management: A no hype guide for teams


Events

  • Association for Intelligent information Management AI+IM Summit | March 31- April 2 (Atlanta)

  • Microsoft 365 Community Conference | May 5-8, 2025 (Vegas)

  • European Collaboration Summit | May 26-28, 2025 (Düsseldorf, Germany)

  • TechCon 365 Seattle | June 23-27, 2025 (Seattle)

 

Production

bodyHtml:

Dennis has been leading the charge for introducing modern marketing – podcasts – to help small law firms promote their unique expertise and connect with their clients. He’s a pioneer in using modern Web3 marketing techniques to connect professional services firms.


In this episode, Dennis dives deep into the latest trends in marketing, shedding light on how businesses can navigate these new waters to achieve greater success.



Dennis shares his insights on:

  • The rise of data-driven marketing strategies and how they can be leveraged to gain a competitive edge.

  • The importance of personalized customer experiences in building brand loyalty and driving sales.

  • The growing influence of social media influencers and how to effectively collaborate with them.


Tune in to explore these topics in more detail and discover actionable strategies that can help you transform your marketing efforts. Don't miss this chance to learn from one of the industry's leading voices.


Polaris is available on Apple, Spotify, Amazon, YouTube or wherever you get your favorite podcasts. Thanks.

He explores the importance of influencer marketing, the role of podcasting in building authority, and how attorneys can leverage digital platforms to connect with their ideal clients. Dennis also shares insights on simplifying the podcasting process for lawyers, the significance of specialization, and the future of marketing in a rapidly changing digital landscape.


Keywords

modern marketing, professional services, legal industry, podcasting, branding, influencer marketing, digital marketing, content creation, Web3, AI


Takeaways

  • Modern marketing techniques are essential for professional services.

  • Podcasting can significantly enhance a lawyer's authority and reach.

  • Attorneys need to embrace digital marketing to stay competitive.

  • Specialization in legal practice areas is crucial for success.

  • Earning attention is more effective than traditional advertising.

  • The future of marketing involves embracing new technologies and AI.

  • Podcasting should be viewed as a means to generate client engagement, not just views.

title: Polaris: AI and the Digital Workplace with Ed Rogers from Akumina and Michelle Caldwell
excerpt: On Polaris, we explore AI and the digital workplace with Ed Rogers, CEO of Akumina and Michelle Caldwell.
bodyHtml:
Digital workplaces are no longer a distant reality; they are here, transforming how we communicate, collaborate, and drive productivity.


In this special episode of Polaris, we explore the interplay between AI and the digital workplace with our guests, Ed Rogers, CEO of Akumina, and Michelle Caldwell, CEO of Synozur. In our original discussion of digital workspaces, we had such an extensive discussion about AI that we’re publishing it as its own special episode (a “Polaris Pulse”.)


Digital workplaces are virtual work environments that combine technology, people, and business processes to drive communication, collaboration, and productivity.


Akumina creates digital employee hubs that deliver:

  • Effortless communication with unified solutions for news and information

  • Tools to integrate apps and tools that boost productivity

  • Streamlined processes that boost operational efficiency


Our Speakers:

Ed Rogers - CEO and co-founder of Akumina: Ed has a rich history of helping business leaders change the way they do business. Before Akumina, he was the COO of Ektron, a leader in the web content management space. Ed is a member of the New Hampshire CEO consortium and is passionate about hockey and spending time with his four children.


Michelle Caldwell – CEO and co-founder of Synozur: With over 25 years of experience, Michelle excels in spearheading business transformations. Her strategic guidance and impactful advice have been instrumental in shaping executive steering committees, refining annual strategies, and enhancing operational frameworks. An esteemed global speaker on operational design and employee engagement, Michelle is based in the Pacific Northwest.

Here are the highlights of our discussion:


The Transformative Power of AI

AI is revolutionizing digital workplaces by automating routine tasks, providing data-driven insights, and enhancing decision-making processes. Ed and Michelle emphasized that AI should be leveraged to augment human capabilities rather than replace them. They highlighted the importance of maintaining a human-centric approach while integrating AI technologies to ensure that employees feel empowered and engaged.


Strategies for Effective AI Integration

Integrating AI into digital workplaces requires a cohesive strategy that aligns with the organization’s goals and values. Ed and Michelle discussed the need for a comprehensive approach that includes:

  • Employee Training: Providing employees with the necessary training and resources to use AI tools effectively.

  • Change Management: Implementing change management practices to address employee concerns and ensure a smooth transition.

  • Collaboration: Encouraging collaboration between IT and business units to identify the most impactful use cases for AI.

Avoiding Fragmentation

One of the challenges in digital workplaces is the fragmentation of digital tools and platforms, which can hinder productivity and user experience. Ed and Michelle stressed the importance of having cohesive strategies that ensure seamless integration of various digital tools. This approach helps avoid silos and ensures that employees have a unified and efficient work environment.

The Role of Omni AI

Omni-AI, or the integration of AI across multiple platforms and touchpoints, is essential for creating a consistent and cohesive digital experience. Ed and Michelle explained how omni-AI can enhance productivity by providing employees with intelligent insights and recommendations regardless of the platform they are using, fostering a more inclusive and collaborative digital workplace.

 

Join Us for our Next Webinar

We invite you to join us live on Tuesday, March 11 for our next webinar, “Transforming Your Digital Workplace” with Michelle and Ed.  We’ll include live demos and Q&A as we explore the evolution of digital workplaces in the AI world.

Transforming Your Digital Workplace: Insights and Strategies | Tuesday, March 11, 2025 8:00AM PST (Online) 


Register Now

Polaris is available on Apple, Spotify, Amazon, YouTube or wherever you get your favorite podcasts. Thanks.

Show Notes

Welcome to a special episode of Polaris Pulse, where we’re joined by Ed Rogers of Akumina and Michelle Caldwell to explore the transformative impact of AI on digital workplaces, discussing the challenges and strategies for effective integration. AI offers new ways to generate and consume information in the digital workplace, while digital workplace tools can unify fragmented user experiences that are a byproduct of a multiplying range of AI systems. Together, they unravel the challenges and strategies necessary for creating cohesive and productive digital workplaces, emphasizing the crucial balance between technology, people, and processes.


Keywords

AI, digital workplace, productivity, omni-AI, employee engagement, chatbots, organizational culture

Takeaways

  • The proliferation of AI tools is reshaping digital workplaces. Task switching among AI applications is a significant productivity drain.

  • Digital workplaces must integrate technology, people, and processes effectively.

  • AI is not just a tool; it's a strategic necessity for businesses.

  • A cohesive strategy is needed for integrating various AI systems.

  • The human element remains vital in AI interactions.

  • Organizations must avoid fragmentation in their digital tools.

  • AI should enhance human interaction, not replace it.


Sound Bites

  • "AI is not just a tool; it's a partner that can enhance our creativity and productivity, making digital workplaces more dynamic and efficient." - Ed Rogers

  • "Integrating AI in the workplace is not just about automation; it's about creating an environment where innovation flourishes." - Michelle Caldwell

References

  • AI continues to grow. Synozur research is projecting the market for generative AI is growing at triple digit rates and we'll reach significantly over $100 billion in 2025. But that expansion of revenues is also leading to an expansion of interfaces.

  • AI proliferation contributing to productivity declines: Synozur research, based in part on data from Harvard Business Revie, shows that the productivity drain from knowledge worker task switching will reach a staggering $279.5 billion this year.  Embracing the Future: Predictions for AI in 2025 — The Synozur Alliance

 

Events

  • Transforming the Digital Workplace – Webinar. On March 11, join Ed Rogers and Michelle Caldwell for a live webinar exploring digital workplaces in depth, with demos and resources. 


Production

bodyHtml:
Marketing is big. In the United States alone, there are 2.5 million marketers, and 6 million counting marketing-adjacent roles like sales, public relations, fundraising, user experience, and graphic design. Those numbers will continue to grow faster than the rest of the economy over the next seven years.[1]



 

So, what are all these people doing and spending? What is marketing, really? And what does success look like? That’s the subject of this series.

 

Delivering and Leading Marketing

Marketing can be hard to define, but you know it when you see it. Even within marketing teams, terms like "inbound" and "GTM" can have different meanings.

 

Once you understand what marketing is, the next questions are how to deliver and lead it. These are some of the questions I'll answer in this four-article series:


  • Marketing in the 21st Century: A New Definition

  • New Directions for Inbound and Outbound Marketing

  • How to Be a Successful Marketer - Actions and Values

  • How to Be a Successful Marketing Leader – Principles and Culture

 

A Note on My Experience

My professional career has been in large-scale commercial marketing, primarily business-to-business. While many concepts apply to consumer marketing, there are clear differences in customer journey and value. This series is focused on commercial, B2B marketing.

 

Marketing Defined

Throughout my career at Microsoft, Dell, John Hancock, Banco Santander, and more, I've worked in and alongside marketing in many leadership roles. However, I've never found a commonly agreed definition of "marketing." Over a decade ago, I used "marketing" and "advertising" as synonyms in conference presentations, which wasn't fair to either discipline.

 

I've seen conflict and misalignment due to differing definitions of marketing. My teams at Microsoft cam quote me that their job is not (just) to be the promotions crew for a set of feature developers. It’s a lot more than that.

 

But what is “more”?


Marketing busywork

Increasingly, “more” means AI. In 2024, AI usage among marketers rose at a staggering rate. Marketers reported using AI tools for various purposes, including content creation (43%), research (34%), brainstorming (27%), learning how to do things (40%), data analysis/reporting (35%), and taking notes or summarizing meetings (27%)[2].

 

And on average, marketing budgets make up 10% of overall company budgets.[3] And that adds up. In 2023, advertising and marketing spending worldwide grew by around five percent to over $US 1.65 trillion.[4]  

 

“The CMO is coming, look busy” is a recipe for career and marketing failure. Marketing actions without purpose and intent won’t work. Nor will random AI experiments that ignore marketing’s true mission.


  A lot of marketing energy goes for naught. According to Claravine, 25% of marketing campaigns have been negatively impacted by poor data management, and 37% of marketing spend is wasted due to poor data quality and inaccurate targeting, resulting in a 30% loss of customers[5].

 

Marketing (Re)defined

It's high time to build a Marketing & Positioning Framework (MPF) for marketing itself – identifying stakeholders, positioning, core messages, and value propositions. Later in the series, I’ll discuss the importance of messaging and positioning for a product.

 

In business school at BC, a professor told me that only marketing and product development create customer value. Product development creates what customers buy, and marketing delivers innovation and education to customers. While helpful, that view is incomplete.

 

A well-known marketing cheerleader at Microsoft says, "Marketing turns technologies into businesses." It’s a great summary but lacks detail on the "how."

 

Simply put, marketing connects markets to products and brings products to markets.

 

As a marketer, your job is to bring customer insights and needs into the product and bring those products, solutions, or offerings back to the market. The market is big – it includes customers, partners, press, analysts, sales, support, and more.


The Marketing Mission in the Modern Organization

Let’s turn that into a statement. And one that works across industries. What does marketing do?


Marketing has primary responsibility for developing and delivering the brand and the products to all key channels and stakeholders, and is the decision-maker on naming, messaging, and long-term offering strategy.

Marketing doesn't build the product but influences its direction and takes innovation from the lab to the customer.

 

Marketing is responsible for "the business" but is often less staffed than sales, product, or manufacturing groups. It needs to be engaged in all parts of the value chain, including channel partners, journalists, sales teams, and finance – but without over engaging and becoming a bottleneck to other critical allied actions.

 


Marketing needs to be insanely curious about customers. Customer experience begins before a product is purchased or even known. Details like pricing and naming are the first steps in conveying value and establishing perceptions. My undergraduate sociology professor often discussed the price of beer as a value message. If it's priced at $1 per six-pack, it seems low quality; if it's $100 per six-pack, it's too expensive. It doesn’t matter how great it is.

 

Naming and messaging create the perception of value throughout the customer journey. Time to value, quality, precision, and results all matter. But in the end, emotional appeal – intrigue, curiosity, and delight – can elevate a single transaction into a lifelong relationship.

 

That’s harder than it sounds. When NFL teams trade a popular player, we often hear it’s “just doing business.” Feelings aren’t supposed to matter. But to drive customer engagement, they’re essential.

 

Evolving Business Models

Business models are evolving away from single point-in-time transactions. Increasingly, purchases may be subscriptions, consumption-based pricing, or ongoing usage goals. As a marketer, you need to stay curious and engaged throughout the full customer journey, partnering with sales teams, customer success groups, and channel partners. And you need to connect to customers through direct engagement, group reviews, online presentations, and more.

 

Marketing activities include events, blogs, social media, and email campaigns, along with emerging media like short-form video or podcasts. In the next article, we'll discuss the actions and attributes of a successful marketer. But for now, marketing is defined by its ability to connect market needs to the business and bring offerings to the market.

 

Closing

Thanks for reading this far. In part two, we’ll look in detail at the ebb and flow of “inbound” and “outbound” and redefine those terms for 21st century marketing.

 


[1] Marketing Industry Stats and Information

[2] The 2025 State of Marketing & Trends Report: Data from 1700+ Global Marketers (Hubspot)

[3] Marketing Industry Stats and Information

[4] Marketing worldwide – statistics & facts | Statista

[5] Avoid Wasting Millions on Useless Digital Ad Campaign Spend (Claravine, 2021)

Marketing is responsible for "the business" but is often less staffed than sales, product, or manufacturing groups. It needs to be engaged in all parts of the value chain, including channel partners, journalists, sales teams, and finance – but without over engaging and becoming a bottleneck to other critical allied actions.

  

Marketing needs to be insanely curious about customers. Customer experience begins before a product is purchased or even known. Details like pricing and naming are the first steps in conveying value and establishing perceptions. My undergraduate sociology professor often discussed the price of beer as a value message. If it's priced at $1 per six-pack, it seems low quality; if it's $100 per six-pack, it's too expensive. It doesn’t matter how great it is.

Naming and messaging create the perception of value throughout the customer journey. Time to value, quality, precision, and results all matter. But in the end, emotional appeal – intrigue, curiosity, and delight – can elevate a single transaction into a lifelong relationship.

That’s harder than it sounds. When NFL teams trade a popular player, we often hear it’s “just doing business.” Feelings aren’t supposed to matter. But to drive customer engagement, they’re essential.

## Evolving Business Models

Business models are evolving away from single point-in-time transactions. Increasingly, purchases may be subscriptions, consumption-based pricing, or ongoing usage goals. As a marketer, you need to stay curious and engaged throughout the full customer journey, partnering with sales teams, customer success groups, and channel partners. And you need to connect to customers through direct engagement, group reviews, online presentations, and more.

Marketing activities include events, blogs, social media, and email campaigns, along with emerging media like short-form video or podcasts. In the next article, we'll discuss the actions and attributes of a successful marketer. But for now, marketing is defined by its ability to connect market needs to the business and bring offerings to the market.

## Closing

Thanks for reading this far. In part two, we’ll look in detail at the ebb and flow of “inbound” and “outbound” and redefine those terms for 21st century marketing.

We dive into the future of digital workplaces with our guests, Ed Rogers, CEO of Akumina, and Michelle Caldwell, CEO of Synozur. Our discussion focuses on the key trends and strategies shaping the digital workplace landscape in 2025.

Intranets, Microsoft Teams, and Google Workspace are all part of these experiences.

Akumina is a pioneer in delivering digital employee hubs that deliver:

  • Effortless communication with unified solutions for news and information

  • Tools to integrate apps and tools that boost productivity

  • Streamlined processes that boost operational efficiency


Our Speakers:

Ed Rogers - CEO and co-founder of Akumina: Ed has a rich history of helping business leaders change the way they do business. Before Akumina, he was the COO of Ektron, a leader in the web content management space. Ed is a member of the New Hampshire CEO consortium and is passionate about hockey and spending time with his four children.


Michelle Caldwell – CEO and co-founder of Synozur: With over 25 years of experience, Michelle excels in spearheading business transformations. Her strategic guidance and impactful advice have been instrumental in shaping executive steering committees, refining annual strategies, and enhancing operational frameworks. An esteemed global speaker on operational design and employee engagement, Michelle is based in the Pacific Northwest.

I had a great discussion with Michelle and Ed about how they're responding to customer needs with a focus on employee engagement, two-way conversation, and high-quality content.

  • Transforming Internal Communications: Ed and Michelle discussed the pivotal role of news and internal communications in creating an engaging digital workplace.

  • Driving Employee Engagement: Michelle and Ed also connected employee engagement to employee effectiveness and organizational success.

title: Achieving Strategic HR Impact with Empathetic Workplace Experiences
excerpt: CHROs are looking to rebuild the HR operating model to enable agility, strategic alignment, and operational efficiency.
bodyHtml:
Today's CEOs expect transformational growth while navigating economic volatility, competitive labor markets, emerging technologies like AI, and evolving employee expectations. To meet these challenges, CHROs are looking to rebuild the HR operating model to enable agility, strategic alignment, and operational efficiency. This transformation requires a partner that understands both the intricacies of the employee experience and the capabilities of modern workplace tools.


Synozur, with its focus on the employee experience and deep knowledge of the Microsoft ecosystem, positions itself as a valuable ally for CHROs seeking to enhance their strategic impact. Synozur aims to guide organizations in building new experiences for communications, collaboration, and productivity, which drives efficiency, engagement, employee satisfaction, and business value. 


Addressing HR's Challenges

According to Gartner, 87% of HR leaders believe that shifting business needs require continuous HR transformation. Many HR functions have restructured or plan to restructure to address these needs. However, only 24% of HR leaders believe their current HR structure appropriately separates transactional and strategic tasks.


To help HR increase its strategic impact, Gartner suggests a new operating model, built around four imperatives: 


  1. Building a robust HR operations and service delivery team: This centralized team, led by an HR chief operations officer, focuses on servicing employees and managers to lay the operational foundation for strategic impact.

  2. Reinventing the HR business partner (HRBP) to be a strategic talent leader: These leaders align with business units, acting as de facto CHROs and partnering with business leaders to address pressing business challenges. Sample actions to reimagine HRBPs include outlining strategically focused roles, assessing HRBP skills and interests, and evolving strategic competencies.

  3. Creating a dynamic pool of HR problem solvers: These professionals apply project management and critical thinking skills to short-term HR-related projects. Sample actions include defining team roles and competencies and creating a project charter and prioritization method.

  4. Providing agile support with leaner next-generation centers of excellence (COEs): These COEs focus on creating and upgrading policies, processes, and philosophies. Sample actions to provide agile support include defining the value proposition for next-generation COEs, reevaluating COE activities based on end-user value, and updating COE staffing to drive efficiency and impact.


Synozur can help CHROs implement these imperatives by providing the vision, strategy, and design needed to make the desirable achievable. 


Synozur's Approach

At Synozur we emphasize an empathetic approach to modern workplace experiences. They apply a human-centered approach, leading with an understanding of people to inform the Employee Effectiveness Journey. Our approach involves:

  • Dream it: Delivering the vision, strategy, and design.

  • Build it: Taking a human-centered approach by understanding people.

  • Grow it: Customizing services based on specific needs.


We leverage our expertise in the Microsoft ecosystem to help our clients navigate the complexities of modern workplace technology. Synozur’s alliance of experts provides insights and results, drawing on deep knowledge of Microsoft platforms, products, and tools. We understand how Microsoft's tools can meet customer needs. As Microsoft MVPs and RDs, Synozur has strong connections within Microsoft's product teams, offering a unique perspective on the future of Microsoft platforms.


Strategic Alignment and Employee Experience

A core element of increasing HR's strategic impact is aligning HR strategy with business goals. Gartner recommends evaluating HR's effectiveness against both HR's own goals and the goals of the business. This involves understanding what the business expects from HR and identifying high-priority improvement areas. 


Our focus on the employee experience aligns with the need for HR to address changing employee expectations and create a positive work environment. By designing dynamic employee journeys that encompass the entire employee lifecycle, organizations can improve employee well-being, productivity, and innovation. Synozur's methods apply to various types of employees, including knowledge workers, frontline workers, field workers, full-time employees, contractors, and vendors.


Measuring Impact

To ensure the success of HR transformation efforts, it's crucial to measure the impact of systematic design of the employee journey. Gartner suggests evaluating HR's effectiveness against its goals and the goals of the business to identify areas for improvement. By establishing clear criteria for successful strategy execution, HR can measure progress, identify bottlenecks, and focus efforts to maximize performance. 


Our focus on driving efficiency, engagement, employee satisfaction, and business value provide a framework for measuring the impact of its solutions. By working with Synozur, CHROs can gain insights into how to create a service ecosystem for employees and evaluate the current employee experience to identify gaps.

title: DeepThoughts on Deep Seek
excerpt: Chinese startup DeepSeek has announced a credible alternative to ChatGPT, challenging the GenAI market.
bodyHtml:
(cowritten with Chris McNulty)


If you haven’t heard the latest news about DeepSeek and its impact on the GenAI market today, take a look.  A Chinese startup, DeepSeek, has annouced a credible alternative to ChatGPT using open source and fewer Nvidia chips than expected.


Is China's AI tool DeepSeek as good as it seems? | BBC 


In that spirit, we also wanted to share some new analyst research from Alan Pelz-Sharpe at Deep Analysis. (Their monthly newsletter is a great source for public research.)

The Generative AI bubble is bursting in real-time. | Deep Analysis


DeepSeek is absolutely moving at warp speed across the indsutry. Today at Microsoft’s AI Tour in New York, Scott Guthrie annouced that Microsoft is now offering DeepMind AI models as part of Azure AI Foundry and GitHub (joining the other 1700+ AI models supported by Microsoft.)  For more, see: DeepSeek R1 is now available on Azure AI Foundry and GitHub


Apart from the immediate impact on certain tech stocks (NVidia dropped 17.44% on Monday), it’s not clear in the long run if DeepSeek, specifically will be a lasting answer to customer demands for cheaper, faster AI. But those demands will only grow louder moving forward.



It’s unlikely that Western companies will move en masse to hand over their sensitive data and IP to a China-based AI service - look at the history with TikTok. Observers have also raised legitimate questions about DeepSeek’s data handling and privacy policies.  But the price pressure, given what's suggested with standard chipsets and open-source LLMs, will be a real thing. At a minimum, this will freeze some deals and disrupt buyer decisions.

In the end, this may just be more FUD (Fear Uncertainty and Doubt) in a highly competitive AI market. We don’t yet know if DeepSeek is really running on cheap chips and open source as much as they’ve disclosed, so the next week will be interesting.

Emerging Considerations

An interesting and cautionary POV has emerged regarding the possibility that all the fuss about DeepSeek is actually a Chinese government-orchestrated psychological operation (psyop). DeepSeek's remarkably rapid success and close ties to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) are fueling these suspicions. This blog by @Amuse on Substack [editor's note: post removed May 2025] assesses DeepSeek's technological advantages, its potential access to restricted resources, its recent impact on the US stock market (NASDAQ down 3.7% Monday, NVIDIA down 16% over the last two trading days), and the inherent cybersecurity and data privacy risks associated with its technology.


Expert opinions vary, highlighting the debate surrounding DeepSeek's true nature and intentions. It's open source and 1/10 the cost of equivalent power from OpenAI, and its performance cannot be ignored:



@mens_aurelius on X posits that it's part of a CCP strategy to undermine the huge infrastructure investments required by the US approach to AI (e.g. the recent StarGate announcements). The end goal would be to encourage the US to deprioritize these investments and convince "investors and boards to shift their focus to chasing an illusion."


#TimeWillTell

title: Polaris Podcast: Fractional CxOs Get Our Undivided Attention
excerpt: Our latest episode of our Polaris podcast, “Fractional CxOs Get Our Undivided Attention" dives into the evolving role of fractional leaders.
bodyHtml:
Our latest episode of our Polaris podcast, “Fractional CxOs Get Our Undivided Attention“dives into the evolving role of fractional executive leaders, or CxOs. We explore why fractional CxOs are becoming more prevalent and what they mean for businesses today.


Our guest is Michelle Caldwell, the CEO and founder of Synozur.


Fractional leadership is an emerging trend that offers cost-effective and flexible solutions for startups and smaller businesses. As of January 2024, over 282,000 LinkedIn users identified as fractional chief marketing officers, reflecting the growing popularity and acceptance of this leadership model.


Since 2016, the term fractional CxO has experienced an exponential boom, with temporary business management roles increasing significantly. From 2021 through 2022, fractional jobs rose by 18%, and they're up over 57% since 2020. This surge is driven by the need for adaptable leadership to navigate the complexities of modern business environments. Our discussion highlights the benefits and challenges of fractional leadership, making this a must-listen episode for anyone interested in the future of executive roles.



You can find Polaris on Apple, Spotify, Amazon, or wherever you get your favorite podcasts. Interested in joining a future episode? Contact us at polaris@synozur.com for more details.  Thanks.

bodyHtml:
Recently, Matt Shaffer, Synozur’s lead for Strategic Planning and Organizational Design presented our “Upgrading our Company Operating System” webinar. He introduced the Company Operating System (CoS), and how it can help you transform your leadership culture in 2025.


Matt covered:

  • What’s a Company Operating System?

  • Why companies may need a new approach

  • Common business strategic challenges

  • Case Study – Management makeover at a luxury brand

  • Getting Started and Recommendations


Watch the Webinar

A Company Operating System is a framework that outlines how a company functions. It includes the foundational building blocks, strategy, plans, goals, and measures across the organization.


A CoS helps create and maintain focus on business priorities, and improves organizational effectiveness by identifying what’s important, keeping leaders and staff focused on those priorities, and tracking the progress of the strategy and plans for an honest evaluation of “is our plan working?”


Just like computers, the CoS is the "operating system" for your business, helping you work together efficiently and effectively.


At Synozur, we use company operating systems as an essential component of transforming business strategy for our clients. You can also learn more from our new white paper Transforming Business Strategy and Operations with Company Operating Systems.


We’d love to hear from you about how we can help you achieve more in 2025. Thanks.

title: Embracing the Future: Predictions for AI in 2025
excerpt: Synozur AI predictions for 2025: "Omni AI" across all platforms, AI agent anxiety, and personal knowledge chatbots stall out.
bodyHtml:
Happy New Year! As we step into 2025, the world of artificial intelligence is changing faster than ever. Generative AI, though still new, has the potential to completely transform how we work. Here at Synozur, we’re watching the trends that will shape AI in the coming year.

Last year, Katya Linossi, CEO of ClearPeople, asked me to share my insights as part of their eBook The Trends Shaping Knowledge in 2025.  (ClearPeople builds enterprise solutions for Microsoft 365 to unlock enterprise knowledge and drive business growth.) It was an honor to be published alongside other industry luminaries. My predictions include:

  • "Omni AI" that works across all platforms

  • Anxiety about powerful AI agents

  • The rise and rise of personal knowledge chatbots


Let’s look at them in more detail:


Omni AI Integration  

Every software vendor is adding or enhancing their AI chat interfaces. Each can generate answers from their unique knowledge store. That’s leading to AI proliferation. If you need to prepare for a client meeting by going into Copilot, Salesforce, ServiceNow and SAP, that’s a lot of context switching. Haven’t we learned past lessons about the cost of task switching? Synozur research, based in part on data from Harvard Business Review[1], shows that the productivity drain from knowledge worker task switching will reach a staggering $279.5 billion this year. 


There’s an emerging path to improve both AI quality and ROI. Businesses will increasingly demand AI that develops answers on data integrated from multiple sources and disconnected AI chatbots, far beyond single-source systems like Gemini and Copilot. Let’s call it “Omni AI.”

Omni AI is based on two approaches which are not mutually exclusive:

  • Content integration. GenAI chatbots need not be limited to a single source if information. Most organizations have dozens of sources of data – a typical $1 billion organization may have more than 50[2]. Customers need a manageable way to create an indexed source of data for LLMs and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation). Microsoft has made some initial steps with its Graph Connectors. I predict an emerging ISV will successfully introduce a next generation solution to unify, enrich and secure cross-platform information for GenAI.

  • Federated chat interfaces. From a user perspective, it doesn’t matter whether their chatbot has a unified “library,” or if it asks a team of other local AI agents to work on their parts of a problem before combining them into a cohesive whole.


Omni AI can create cohesive knowledge systems, empowering better decisions and employee effectiveness. Organizations that adopt Omni AI solutions will experience greater productivity gains than those still using 2023-era AI. 


Anxiety and Skills-Based AI Autonomous Agents 

In 2025, you can expect AI-powered autonomous agents to take digital automation to the next level. These agents will go beyond just managing workflows and robotic process automation (RPA). They’ll handle complex tasks like managing incoming emails to onboard new customers, handling contact management, generating contracts, and scheduling meetings. 


Recently, EY's AI Anxiety in Business Survey revealed that 65% of employees are anxious about AI replacing their job[3]. The fear of AI job disruption will remain much larger than the disruption itself – it’s much harder to automate complex human interactions than we think. But managing that fear will be essential for organizations looking to move quickly to embrace AI solutions. 


Personal Knowledge Chatbots 

In many organizations, our knowledge maps are personal. We try to ask the “best” expert based on what we know they know. For example, Sloane knows the most about the Pittsburgh warehouse design since she’s the manager, so everyone asks her for details.

Personal AI for consumers and business are converging. For example, Character.AI can impersonate anyone – even John F. Kennedy - with a small voice sample, but it doesn’t know or retain anything unique about people. It initially told me I was born in San Jose, CA (Rockville Centre, NY); that I attended University of Georgia and UC Berkeley (see below) and that had three children – Connor, Keegan & Ellie. In 2025, business AI like Microsoft Copilot will it easy to configure an agent that’s grounded on your unique digital workplace footprint (email, chats, documents, meetings etc.), blended with external sources like LinkedIn or even Ancestry.com. These agents will remain a curiosity in 2025. 


Wrapping Up

title: Holiday Reflections from Synozur: A Dynamic 2024
excerpt: Join us in reflecting on 2024 with our latest Polaris episode, "Holiday Reflections from Synozur" - plus our free holiday meal planner!
bodyHtml:
As we near the end of 2024, it's time to take a moment to reflect on the significant events and innovations that have shaped our year. Our latest Polaris podcast, Holiday Reflections from Synozur: A Dynamic 2024, brings together voices from across Synozur to discuss the challenges and triumphs of the past twelve months and to share our predictions for the future.


We’re grateful for our journey with you throughout 2024. That’s why we’ve included a very special and untraditional holiday gift for you – right at the end of this post. Keep reading for more.


A Year of Innovation and Culture

In this special holiday episode of Polaris, hosted by Chris McNulty, we’re joined by Michelle Caldwell, Michelle Boyd, Josh Brantley, Stephen Rose, and Andrew Borg. Together, we delve into key moments in business and technology throughout 2024.



We asked everyone four questions and have included summaries here – and a bit of a holiday reading list. (For the full discussion, please listen to Polaris.)


Highlight from the worlds of technology and business

Michelle Caldwell highlighted advancements in enhanced geothermal systems, and their commercial potential for clean energy. Michelle Boyd was fascinated by images from the James Webb Space Telescope. Stephen Rose and Josh Brantley discussed AI's growing deployment and the gap between expectations and business value. Andrew Borg emphasized the need for ethical AI and aligning technology with human rights. And everyone commented on the midyear CrowdStrike outage and the need to modernize legacy server infrastructure.

  • Enhanced Geothermal Systems: See MIT Technology Review for more information.

  • James Webb Space Telescope: Launched in 2021, the Webb provided unprecedented clarity in astronomy with stunning images of distant galaxies and exoplanet atmospheres. The image below shows the Sombrero Galaxy in photographs from the Webb – compared with an image from its predecessor, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990. For more background, see NASA's Webb Depicts Staggering Structure in 19 Nearby Spiral Galaxies.




Highlights of Synozur’s work in 2024

The team had a lot to consider. Three highlights:

  • Clients: We deployed a new Company Operating System for one of our luxury brand clients who had outgrown their early days as a founder-led business. You can learn more here: Management Makeover at a Luxury Brand.

  • Conference Experiences: It was great to engage with hundreds of customers and community members at events like M365 Community Conference in May, and TechCon 365 Dallas in November. We’re looking forward to even more online and live events in 2025.

  • Polaris Pathways: We launched our inaugural podcast this year.


Favorite moments in food, music, culture, travel, books, films - anything!

Our team also reflected on their personal highlights from 2024, sharing moments and events that left a lasting impression.

  • Coldplay's Music Video "All My Love":  Performing legend Dick Van Dyke turned 99 this month, capping a career that includes his eponymous comedy with Mary Tyler Moore, Mary Poppins, and dancing his way through Coldplay’s heartfelt video highlighting his nine-decade career and his family.

Dick Van Dyke sings with Coldplay's Chris Martin in 'All My Love' music video


  • Olympics 2024: Memorable moments included Snoop Dogg's hosting, and the debut of breakdancing as an Olympic sport. View Snoop Dogg’s BEST MOMENTS At The 2024 Paris Olympics to revisit more.

  • Shogun TV Series on Hulu: No, not the 1980 original. The new series presented a compelling depiction of Japanese culture and its intersection with Western culture. Learn more at Shōgun: The brutal Japanese history that inspired 2024's latest TV hit.

  • Anora (2024 film): An exotic dancer's trouble with the Russian mafia, both hilarious and heartbreaking.  Winner of the 2024 Palme d'Or at Cannes and an early Oscar favorite, it’s available now on digital platforms like Prime Video, Apple TV+, and Fandango. See: Anora - Wikipedia.

  • Excel World Championships: Exactly what that sounds like – a global competition showcasing the advanced use of the ubiquitous spreadsheet platform. Stephen Rose judged this year’s championships in Las Vegas, which also created new opportunities for young women to break into technology. The event was broadcast on ESPN Ocho, and you can learn more at Microsoft Excel World Championship – FMWC.

And of course, travel. Some of our favorite travel highlights this year included multiple opportunities to experience the aurora borealis:

·       Olympic Mountains

·       Breckenridge, Colorado

·       Iceland

·       Whidbey Island


Hopes and predictions for 2025

  • AI Agents: We’re waiting for new AI agents for common needs like project management or employee self-service, as highlighted during the Ignite conference.

  • Rise of Fractional Expertise: Due to ongoing layoffs and restructuring, a nearly unprecedented amount of senior talent – previously out of reach – is becoming available to many organizations as “fractional CXOs”.

  • Skepticism and Business Value of AI: Growing skepticism around AI and the need for businesses to focus on the actual value AI brings to balance the hype cycle.

Join the Conversation

Tune in to Polaris and share your thoughts on the year we've had and your hopes for 2025 at polaris@synozur.com. Let's continue to explore and embrace the exciting opportunities that lie ahead.

Holiday Gift – Synozur Meal Planner

Yes, you read that right!


As we wrap up 2024, we’re happy to share a special – and atypical - holiday gift with you! Our Synozur Holiday Meal Planner is here to help you plan and track every detail of your holiday meal, from boiling potatoes to resting the roast. With easy-to-follow directions and customizable inputs, you can ensure everything is perfectly timed for your family feast. Check out our blog post for more details and download the planner to make your holiday meal preparation a breeze.


Thanks again. Best wishes for a happy and peaceful holiday season, and see you in 2025!
